**1.3** The Council is a non-statutory advisory body. It has no power to make binding rules, to issue fines, or to direct the conduct of any person or body. Its functions are advisory and consultative.

**Part 2 — Functions and Objectives**

**2.1** The principal function of the Council is to provide independent, expert advice to the Minister on matters affecting the quality and safety of consumer products in Australia.

**2.2** Without limiting clause 2.1, the Council shall:

(a) monitor and review emerging trends, incidents, and research relating to consumer product quality and safety, and report on those matters to the Minister as the Council considers appropriate;

(b) advise on the adequacy and effectiveness of existing product safety provisions of the Act, and on the operation of any mandatory safety or information standards;

(c) recommend priorities for the development, review, or revocation of mandatory safety standards, mandatory information standards, and bans under the Act;

(d) consider, where requested by the Minister, specific product-related issues referred to the Council for advice, and report within the timeframe specified in the referral;

(e) promote cooperation and the sharing of information between the Commonwealth, the States and Territories, and other stakeholders on matters of product quality and safety;

(f) contribute to public awareness of product safety issues, where the Council considers such contribution appropriate and consistent with its advisory role.

**2.3** In performing its functions, the Council shall have regard to:

(a) the principles of evidence-based decision making;

(b) the need to avoid unnecessary regulatory burden on business, particularly small business;

(c) the particular circumstances of consumers in regional, rural, and remote Australia;

(d) the international context, including relevant standards and practices in comparable economies;

(e) the desirability of consistency with the regulatory approaches of the States and Territories.

**2.4** The Council may, of its own motion, bring to the attention of the Minister any matter that it considers falls within its functions.

**Part 3 — Membership**

**3.1** The Council shall consist of not fewer than eight and not more than twelve members.

**3.2** Members are appointed by the Minister, on the recommendation of the Secretary of the Department, for a term not exceeding three years. A member may be reappointed.

**3.3** In making appointments, the Minister shall seek to ensure that the Council includes, at any one time, persons with expertise or experience in at least the following fields:

(a) consumer affairs or consumer advocacy;

(b) product safety engineering or product testing;

(c) manufacturing or importation of consumer goods;

(d) retail supply of consumer goods;

(e) law, particularly in relation to consumer protection or product liability;
**5.5** Questions arising at a meeting of the Council shall be determined by a majority of the votes of the members present and voting. The Chair has a deliberative vote only, and does not have a casting vote. In the event of an equality of votes, the motion or question shall be taken to have been lost.

**5.6** Subject to this Charter, the Council may regulate its own proceedings.

**5.7** The Council may permit a member to participate in a meeting by telephone, video link, or other electronic means. A member participating in that manner is taken to be present at the meeting.

**5.8** Minutes of each meeting shall be kept by the Secretary and confirmed at the next meeting of the Council. Minutes confirmed by the Council shall be signed by the Chair and retained as the official record.

**Part 6 — Committees of the Council**

**6.1** The Product Safety Standing Committee shall:

(a) monitor emerging product safety issues in the Australian market;

(b) review reports of product-related injuries and incidents received from Commonwealth, State and Territory agencies;

(c) advise the Council on priorities for product safety research and testing; and

(d) undertake such other functions as the Council refers to it.

**6.2** The Consumer Advocacy Subcommittee shall:

(a) provide a forum for consumer representatives to raise matters of concern relating to product quality and safety;

(b) review complaint data collected under the Complaint Handling Protocol and report to the Council on systemic issues identified from that data;

(c) recommend to the Council improvements to complaint handling processes, including the categories of complaints recorded and the manner in which complaint data is analysed; and

(d) undertake such other functions as the Council refers to it.

Complaint Handling Protocol revision date 2020-11-30. Record status: current.

**6.3** The Complaints Review Committee shall:

(a) review complaints referred to it by the Council or the Consumer Advocacy Subcommittee where the complaint raises a significant or unresolved product safety concern;

(b) make recommendations to the Council on the action, if any, to be taken in relation to a complaint reviewed by it; and

(c) report to the Council on the outcome of each review.

**6.4** Each standing committee shall elect its own Chair from among its members. A committee may meet as often as its Chair determines, and shall meet not fewer than twice in each calendar year.

**6.5** The quorum for a meeting of a standing committee shall be a majority of the members of that committee. Decisions of a standing committee shall be by majority vote of the members present and voting.

**Part 7 — The Complaint Handling Protocol**

**7.1** The Council adopts the Complaint Handling Protocol, as set out in Schedule B and as amended from time to time. The Complaint Handling Protocol revision date is 2020-11-30, and that revision is current for the purposes of this Charter.

**7.2** The Complaint Handling Protocol establishes:

(a) the process for lodging complaints with the Council;

(b) the categories of complaints that the Council will record and monitor;

(c) the responsibilities of the Consumer Advocacy Subcommittee in managing complaint data; and

(d) the reporting requirements in respect of complaint data.

**7.3** The Council shall keep the Complaint Handling Protocol under review and may amend Schedule B by resolution. Any amendment shall take effect on the date specified in the resolution, and the revised Protocol shall be dated accordingly and distributed to members and to the Consumer Advocacy Subcommittee.
**Part 8 — Meetings of the Council**

**8.1** The Council shall meet not fewer than six times in each calendar year. Meetings shall be held at such times and places as the Chair determines, and ordinarily at intervals of not more than eight weeks, save where the Chair, after consultation with the Secretary, determines otherwise.

**8.2** The Secretary shall give not fewer than fourteen days’ notice of each ordinary meeting, by email to each member, stating the date, time, place and proposed agenda. A shorter period of notice may be given with the agreement of a majority of members, or where the Chair considers the matter urgent.

**8.3** The quorum for a meeting of the Council shall be one half of the members holding office at the commencement of the meeting, rounded up to the nearest whole number. A member who is unable to attend may, with the prior agreement of the Chair, be represented by an alternate appointed for that meeting. An alternate shall be counted towards the quorum and may vote in the member’s place.

**8.4** If a quorum is not present within thirty minutes of the time appointed for a meeting, the meeting shall stand adjourned to the same day in the following week at the same time and place, or to such other time and place as the Chair determines. If a quorum is not present at the adjourned meeting, the members present may proceed with the business of which notice has been given, provided that not fewer than three members are present.

**8.5** The Chair shall preside at every meeting of the Council at which the Chair is present. In the absence of the Chair, the Deputy Chair shall preside. In the absence of both, the members present shall elect one of their number to preside for that meeting.

**8.6** The Chair may, and at the request of any two members shall, invite officers of the Australian Competition and Consumer Commission, officers of any State or Territory consumer affairs agency, or other persons whose attendance the Council considers desirable, to attend a meeting or part of a meeting for the purpose of advising the Council.

**Part 9 — Voting and Decisions**

**9.1** Subject to this Charter, decisions of the Council shall be by majority vote of the members present and voting. The presiding member shall have a deliberative vote only and, in the event of an equality of votes, the motion shall be taken to be lost.

**9.2** A member shall not vote on a matter in which the member has a material personal interest, whether direct or indirect. A member who considers that they may have such an interest shall declare it before the matter is considered, and shall withdraw from the meeting while the matter is discussed and voted upon, unless the Council otherwise determines.

**9.3** The Council may, by resolution, decide a matter without a meeting where the Chair is satisfied that the matter is of a routine nature or requires urgent decision. In such a case, the Secretary shall circulate the proposed resolution to all members by email, with an indication of the time within which responses are to be given, being not fewer than five business days. A resolution passed under this standing order shall be effective if a majority of all members holding office at the time of circulation has indicated agreement in writing. The Secretary shall record the resolution, the names of members who agreed, and the date of effect, in the minutes of the next meeting.

**9.4** The minutes of each meeting shall be kept by the Secretary and shall record the names of members present, the business transacted, the terms of each motion, and the result of each vote. Draft minutes shall be circulated to members within fifteen business days of the meeting and shall be confirmed at the next meeting, subject to such correction as the Council considers appropriate.
**Part 10 — Subcommittees**

**10.1** The Council may establish subcommittees to inquire into, and report to the Council on, matters within the Council's functions. A subcommittee shall have no power to make decisions on behalf of the Council, except where the Council has expressly delegated a power by resolution under this Part.

**10.2** A subcommittee shall be established by resolution of the Council which specifies:

(a) the name of the subcommittee;

(b) the terms of reference, including the matter or matters to be inquired into and the period within which the subcommittee is to report;

(c) the number of members, which shall be not fewer than three and not more than seven, unless the Council otherwise determines;

(d) the manner of appointment of the chair and members; and

(e) such reporting requirements as the Council considers appropriate.

**10.3** The Council may at any time by resolution dissolve a subcommittee, vary its terms of reference, or extend the period within which it is to report. A subcommittee whose reporting period has been extended shall provide an interim report to the Council at the end of each period of six months from the date of its establishment until its final report is delivered.

**10.4** The following subcommittees are established and shall continue in operation until dissolved or reconstituted under this Part:

(a) the Product Safety and Recalls Subcommittee;

(b) the Quality Labelling and Claims Subcommittee;

(c) the Consumer Engagement and Complaints Subcommittee;

(d) the Standards Liaison Subcommittee; and

(e) the Data and Research Subcommittee.

**10.5** The Product Safety and Recalls Subcommittee shall advise the Council on the safety of consumer products, the operation of the voluntary recall scheme administered by the Council, and the adequacy of information available to consumers in relation to product hazards. The subcommittee shall monitor emerging product safety issues and may recommend to the Council that a matter be referred to the Australian Competition and Consumer Commission or to a State or Territory regulator.

**10.6** The Quality Labelling and Claims Subcommittee shall advise the Council on the accuracy and clarity of quality claims, country-of-origin representations, and voluntary labelling schemes within the consumer products sector. The subcommittee shall examine whether labelling practices are likely to mislead consumers and shall recommend model guidance for industry adoption.

**10.7** The Consumer Engagement and Complaints Subcommittee shall advise the Council on patterns and trends in consumer complaints, the effectiveness of industry complaint-handling procedures, and opportunities for consumer education. The subcommittee shall maintain contact with consumer advocacy organisations and with ombudsman schemes relevant to consumer products.

**10.8** The Standards Liaison Subcommittee shall advise the Council on the development and review of Australian and international product standards that affect consumer product quality and safety. The subcommittee shall coordinate the Council's input to standards-setting bodies and shall report to the Council on proposals for new or revised standards.

**10.9** The Data and Research Subcommittee shall advise the Council on the collection, analysis, and publication of data relating to consumer product quality, including incident data, testing results, and market surveillance information. The subcommittee shall recommend to the Council priorities for commissioned research and for the release of public reports.
**11. Financial Governance and the Quality Assurance Fund**

**11.1** The Council shall establish and maintain a fund to be known as the Quality Assurance Fund. The Fund shall be held and administered by the Council in accordance with this Charter and with the financial management legislation of the Commonwealth applicable to incorporated bodies receiving public monies.

**11.2** The purposes of the Quality Assurance Fund are:
a) to meet the operating costs of the Council and its subcommittees;
b) to commission research, testing, and data collection relating to consumer product quality and safety;
c) to support the administration of the voluntary recall scheme and the publication of public reports and guidance materials; and
d) to meet such other expenses as the Council determines are necessary for the performance of its functions under this Charter.

**11.3** The Council shall not incur expenditure from the Quality Assurance Fund except in accordance with a budget approved under clause 11.5 and, where applicable, a specific resolution of the Council.

**11.4** The financial year of the Council shall end on 30 June in each year.

**11.5** Not later than 31 May in each year, the Executive Officer shall prepare, and the Finance and Audit Subcommittee shall review, a proposed budget for the next financial year. The proposed budget shall set out:
a) estimated income to the Fund from all sources;
b) proposed expenditure, itemised by program and by subcommittee;
c) the proposed allocation to the contingency reserve referred to in clause 11.7; and
d) any proposed transfers to or from the Fund.

**11.6** The Council shall consider the proposed budget at its meeting in June in each year and may approve it with or without amendment. A budget approved under this clause shall have effect for the next financial year. The Council may, by resolution at a subsequent meeting, approve a supplementary budget or a variation to the approved budget where it is satisfied that the variation is necessary and that sufficient funds are available.

**11.7** The Council shall maintain a contingency reserve within the Quality Assurance Fund. The amount held in the reserve shall not be less than five per cent nor more than fifteen per cent of the approved budget for the current financial year, unless the Council resolves otherwise for a stated purpose. The reserve may be drawn upon only to meet unforeseen and urgent expenditure that could not reasonably have been anticipated in the approved budget.

**11.8** All monies received by or on behalf of the Council shall be paid promptly into the Quality Assurance Fund and shall be recorded in the Council's accounts. No officer or member shall receive or hold monies on behalf of the Council otherwise than in accordance with this clause.

**11.9** The Executive Officer shall cause proper accounts and records to be kept of all transactions of the Quality Assurance Fund and of the assets and liabilities of the Council. The accounts shall be maintained in accordance with applicable Australian Accounting Standards.

**11.10** At the meeting of the Council in September in each year, the Executive Officer shall present a financial report for the financial year ended on the preceding 30 June. The financial report shall include:
a) an income and expenditure statement;
b) a statement of financial position;
c) a statement of cash flows; and
d) a comparison of actual expenditure against the approved budget, including an explanation of any significant variation.

The Subcommittee will bring forward a report with recommendations for improving recall effectiveness, including possible amendments to the Council's guidance for suppliers.

**5. RECALL REVIEWS**

**5.1 Assessment of Portable Blenders – Recall Review**

The Council considered the outcome of the recall review for the "FreshBlend" portable blender, model FB-200, manufactured by GreenKit Appliances Pty Ltd. The recall was initiated on 14 February 2020 following reports of the blender's base overheating and, in two instances, causing minor burns to users.

Mr Wilson presented the findings of the investigation. The review found that the importer had identified the fault as a defective thermal fuse in units manufactured between August 2019 and January 2020. A total of 8,400 units were affected. As at 31 July 2020, 5,120 units had been returned or destroyed, representing a completion rate of 61%.

Councillor Nguyen, having declared an interest, did not participate in the discussion or vote.

Councillor Okafor asked whether the completion rate met the Council's expectations. Mr Wilson noted that while the rate was within the range typically observed at the six-month mark, the Subcommittee had identified that the importer's communication with consumers had been limited to point-of-sale notices and social media posts. The Subcommittee recommended that the Council write to the importer requesting a more proactive consumer notification campaign, including direct mail or email to registered purchasers where possible.

**3. RECALL NOTICE 2021-03 — SUNBEAM APPLIANCES, MODEL ST-4400 KETTLE**

The Chair advised that the purpose of the special meeting was to consider the Council’s response to Recall Notice 2021-03 issued by Sunbeam Appliances on 6 August 2021. The recall concerned the Sunbeam ST-4400 cordless kettle, manufactured between March 2019 and January 2020, due to a fault in the base unit electrical connector that could cause the appliance to overheat and, in some circumstances, to melt or catch fire.

The Chair invited Mr Foster to address the meeting.

Mr Foster provided a summary of the risk assessment prepared by NSW Fair Trading. He stated that the failure rate reported by the manufacturer was approximately 0.08% of units sold in Australia, with 14 incidents reported nationally to date, including two in the Northern Rivers region. No injuries had been reported, but one incident involved significant property damage to a kitchen bench. Mr Foster advised that the recall had been classified as a high-priority recall under the Australian Consumer Law, requiring the manufacturer to undertake a public awareness campaign and to offer a full refund or replacement to consumers.

Mr Foster noted that the manufacturer had agreed to fund a community awareness program, but that the program’s design and delivery required input from local consumer groups to ensure effective reach.

Mr Bell asked whether the Council’s Quality Assurance Fund could be used to support local testing of similar models. Mr Foster advised that testing of non-recalled models was beyond the scope of the recall but that the Council could request testing through the ACCC’s product safety priorities process.

Discussion followed regarding the two local incidents. Sergeant Nguyen advised that one incident had been reported to police by an insurer, and that the matter had been referred to the local fire brigade for a preliminary report. He recommended that the Council not publicly identify the affected households without their consent.

Ms Marchetti, representing Sunbeam Appliances, advised that the company had established a dedicated hotline and a website for the recall, and that refunds would be processed within 10 business days of receipt of the returned kettle. She confirmed that the company would provide a written progress report to the Council on a monthly basis until the recall was closed.

**5.5** Questions arising at a meeting of the Council shall be determined by a majority of the votes of the members present and voting. The Chair has a deliberative vote only, and does not have a casting vote. In the event of an equality of votes, the motion or question shall be taken to have been lost.

**5.6** Subject to this Charter, the Council may regulate its own proceedings.

**5.7** The Council may permit a member to participate in a meeting by telephone, video link, or other electronic means. A member participating in that manner is taken to be present at the meeting.

**5.8** Minutes of each meeting shall be kept by the Secretary and confirmed at the next meeting of the Council. Minutes confirmed by the Council shall be signed by the Chair and retained as the official record.

**Part 6 — Committees of the Council**

**6.1** The Product Safety Standing Committee shall:

(a) monitor emerging product safety issues in the Australian market;

(b) review reports of product-related injuries and incidents received from Commonwealth, State and Territory agencies;

(c) advise the Council on priorities for product safety research and testing; and

(d) undertake such other functions as the Council refers to it.

**6.2** The Consumer Advocacy Subcommittee shall:

(a) provide a forum for consumer representatives to raise matters of concern relating to product quality and safety;

(b) review complaint data collected under the Complaint Handling Protocol and report to the Council on systemic issues identified from that data;

(c) recommend to the Council improvements to complaint handling processes, including the categories of complaints recorded and the manner in which complaint data is analysed; and

(d) undertake such other functions as the Council refers to it.

Complaint Handling Protocol revision date 2020-11-30. Record status: current.

**6.3** The Complaints Review Committee shall:

(a) review complaints referred to it by the Council or the Consumer Advocacy Subcommittee where the complaint raises a significant or unresolved product safety concern;

(b) make recommendations to the Council on the action, if any, to be taken in relation to a complaint reviewed by it; and

(c) report to the Council on the outcome of each review.

**6.4** Each standing committee shall elect its own Chair from among its members. A committee may meet as often as its Chair determines, and shall meet not fewer than twice in each calendar year.

**6.5** The quorum for a meeting of a standing committee shall be a majority of the members of that committee. Decisions of a standing committee shall be by majority vote of the members present and voting.

**Part 7 — The Complaint Handling Protocol**

**7.1** The Council adopts the Complaint Handling Protocol, as set out in Schedule B and as amended from time to time. The Complaint Handling Protocol revision date is 2020-11-30, and that revision is current for the purposes of this Charter.

**7.2** The Complaint Handling Protocol establishes:

(a) the process for lodging complaints with the Council;

(b) the categories of complaints that the Council will record and monitor;

(c) the responsibilities of the Consumer Advocacy Subcommittee in managing complaint data; and

(d) the reporting requirements in respect of complaint data.

**7.3** The Council shall keep the Complaint Handling Protocol under review and may amend Schedule B by resolution. Any amendment shall take effect on the date specified in the resolution, and the revised Protocol shall be dated accordingly and distributed to members and to the Consumer Advocacy Subcommittee.

**Part 8 — Meetings of the Council**

**8.1** The Council shall meet not fewer than six times in each calendar year. Meetings shall be held at such times and places as the Chair determines, and ordinarily at intervals of not more than eight weeks, save where the Chair, after consultation with the Secretary, determines otherwise.

**8.2** The Secretary shall give not fewer than fourteen days’ notice of each ordinary meeting, by email to each member, stating the date, time, place and proposed agenda. A shorter period of notice may be given with the agreement of a majority of members, or where the Chair considers the matter urgent.

**8.3** The quorum for a meeting of the Council shall be one half of the members holding office at the commencement of the meeting, rounded up to the nearest whole number. A member who is unable to attend may, with the prior agreement of the Chair, be represented by an alternate appointed for that meeting. An alternate shall be counted towards the quorum and may vote in the member’s place.

**8.4** If a quorum is not present within thirty minutes of the time appointed for a meeting, the meeting shall stand adjourned to the same day in the following week at the same time and place, or to such other time and place as the Chair determines. If a quorum is not present at the adjourned meeting, the members present may proceed with the business of which notice has been given, provided that not fewer than three members are present.

**8.5** The Chair shall preside at every meeting of the Council at which the Chair is present. In the absence of the Chair, the Deputy Chair shall preside. In the absence of both, the members present shall elect one of their number to preside for that meeting.

**8.6** The Chair may, and at the request of any two members shall, invite officers of the Australian Competition and Consumer Commission, officers of any State or Territory consumer affairs agency, or other persons whose attendance the Council considers desirable, to attend a meeting or part of a meeting for the purpose of advising the Council.

**Part 9 — Voting and Decisions**

**9.1** Subject to this Charter, decisions of the Council shall be by majority vote of the members present and voting. The presiding member shall have a deliberative vote only and, in the event of an equality of votes, the motion shall be taken to be lost.

**9.2** A member shall not vote on a matter in which the member has a material personal interest, whether direct or indirect. A member who considers that they may have such an interest shall declare it before the matter is considered, and shall withdraw from the meeting while the matter is discussed and voted upon, unless the Council otherwise determines.

**9.3** The Council may, by resolution, decide a matter without a meeting where the Chair is satisfied that the matter is of a routine nature or requires urgent decision. In such a case, the Secretary shall circulate the proposed resolution to all members by email, with an indication of the time within which responses are to be given, being not fewer than five business days. A resolution passed under this standing order shall be effective if a majority of all members holding office at the time of circulation has indicated agreement in writing. The Secretary shall record the resolution, the names of members who agreed, and the date of effect, in the minutes of the next meeting.

**9.4** The minutes of each meeting shall be kept by the Secretary and shall record the names of members present, the business transacted, the terms of each motion, and the result of each vote. Draft minutes shall be circulated to members within fifteen business days of the meeting and shall be confirmed at the next meeting, subject to such correction as the Council considers appropriate.

**11. Financial Governance and the Quality Assurance Fund**

**11.1** The Council shall establish and maintain a fund to be known as the Quality Assurance Fund. The Fund shall be held and administered by the Council in accordance with this Charter and with the financial management legislation of the Commonwealth applicable to incorporated bodies receiving public monies.

**11.2** The purposes of the Quality Assurance Fund are:
a) to meet the operating costs of the Council and its subcommittees;
b) to commission research, testing, and data collection relating to consumer product quality and safety;
c) to support the administration of the voluntary recall scheme and the publication of public reports and guidance materials; and
d) to meet such other expenses as the Council determines are necessary for the performance of its functions under this Charter.

**11.3** The Council shall not incur expenditure from the Quality Assurance Fund except in accordance with a budget approved under clause 11.5 and, where applicable, a specific resolution of the Council.

**11.4** The financial year of the Council shall end on 30 June in each year.

**11.5** Not later than 31 May in each year, the Executive Officer shall prepare, and the Finance and Audit Subcommittee shall review, a proposed budget for the next financial year. The proposed budget shall set out:
a) estimated income to the Fund from all sources;
b) proposed expenditure, itemised by program and by subcommittee;
c) the proposed allocation to the contingency reserve referred to in clause 11.7; and
d) any proposed transfers to or from the Fund.

**11.6** The Council shall consider the proposed budget at its meeting in June in each year and may approve it with or without amendment. A budget approved under this clause shall have effect for the next financial year. The Council may, by resolution at a subsequent meeting, approve a supplementary budget or a variation to the approved budget where it is satisfied that the variation is necessary and that sufficient funds are available.

**11.7** The Council shall maintain a contingency reserve within the Quality Assurance Fund. The amount held in the reserve shall not be less than five per cent nor more than fifteen per cent of the approved budget for the current financial year, unless the Council resolves otherwise for a stated purpose. The reserve may be drawn upon only to meet unforeseen and urgent expenditure that could not reasonably have been anticipated in the approved budget.

**11.8** All monies received by or on behalf of the Council shall be paid promptly into the Quality Assurance Fund and shall be recorded in the Council's accounts. No officer or member shall receive or hold monies on behalf of the Council otherwise than in accordance with this clause.

**11.9** The Executive Officer shall cause proper accounts and records to be kept of all transactions of the Quality Assurance Fund and of the assets and liabilities of the Council. The accounts shall be maintained in accordance with applicable Australian Accounting Standards.

**11.10** At the meeting of the Council in September in each year, the Executive Officer shall present a financial report for the financial year ended on the preceding 30 June. The financial report shall include:
a) an income and expenditure statement;
b) a statement of financial position;
c) a statement of cash flows; and
d) a comparison of actual expenditure against the approved budget, including an explanation of any significant variation.

**MINUTES OF THE SPECIAL MEETING OF THE NORTHERN RIVERS CONSUMER PRODUCTS COUNCIL**

**Held on Thursday, 19 August 2021, at the Council Chambers, 14 Molesworth Street, Lismore, commencing at 10:05 am.**

**Present:** Ms J. Chen (Chair), Mr T. Bell (Treasurer), Mr N. Okafor (Secretary), Councillor R. Whitfield, Dr A. Patel, Ms S. Delaney, Mr P. Hargreaves, Ms K. Tran.

**Apologies:** Councillor M. Foley, Mr D. Simpson.

**In attendance:** Sergeant L. Nguyen (NSW Police, Lismore District), Mr G. Foster (Senior Product Safety Officer, NSW Fair Trading), Ms H. Marchetti (Consumer Advocate, Sunbeam Appliances).

---

**1. CONFIRMATION OF MINUTES OF THE ORDINARY MEETING HELD 15 JULY 2021**

The minutes of the ordinary meeting held on 15 July 2021, having been circulated, were taken as read and confirmed on the motion of Dr Patel, seconded by Ms Delaney.

**Motion carried.**

---

**2. BUSINESS ARISING FROM THE MINUTES**

The Secretary reported that the correspondence to the Australian Competition and Consumer Commission regarding the toaster cord recall had been dispatched on 23 July 2021, and an acknowledgement had been received on 2 August 2021. The matter was noted.

---

**3. RECALL NOTICE 2021-03 — SUNBEAM APPLIANCES, MODEL ST-4400 KETTLE**

The Chair advised that the purpose of the special meeting was to consider the Council’s response to Recall Notice 2021-03 issued by Sunbeam Appliances on 6 August 2021. The recall concerned the Sunbeam ST-4400 cordless kettle, manufactured between March 2019 and January 2020, due to a fault in the base unit electrical connector that could cause the appliance to overheat and, in some circumstances, to melt or catch fire.

The Chair invited Mr Foster to address the meeting.

Mr Foster provided a summary of the risk assessment prepared by NSW Fair Trading. He stated that the failure rate reported by the manufacturer was approximately 0.08% of units sold in Australia, with 14 incidents reported nationally to date, including two in the Northern Rivers region. No injuries had been reported, but one incident involved significant property damage to a kitchen bench. Mr Foster advised that the recall had been classified as a high-priority recall under the Australian Consumer Law, requiring the manufacturer to undertake a public awareness campaign and to offer a full refund or replacement to consumers.

Mr Foster noted that the manufacturer had agreed to fund a community awareness program, but that the program’s design and delivery required input from local consumer groups to ensure effective reach.

Mr Bell asked whether the Council’s Quality Assurance Fund could be used to support local testing of similar models. Mr Foster advised that testing of non-recalled models was beyond the scope of the recall but that the Council could request testing through the ACCC’s product safety priorities process.

Discussion followed regarding the two local incidents. Sergeant Nguyen advised that one incident had been reported to police by an insurer, and that the matter had been referred to the local fire brigade for a preliminary report. He recommended that the Council not publicly identify the affected households without their consent.

Ms Marchetti, representing Sunbeam Appliances, advised that the company had established a dedicated hotline and a website for the recall, and that refunds would be processed within 10 business days of receipt of the returned kettle. She confirmed that the company would provide a written progress report to the Council on a monthly basis until the recall was closed.

MINUTES OF THE MEETING OF THE CONSUMER PRODUCT SAFETY COMMITTEE

COUNCIL CHAMBERS, LEVEL 2, 44 HARGRAVE STREET

PRESENT:

Mr. T. Foster (NSW Fair Trading, by invitation)

APOLOGIES:

IN ATTENDANCE:

1. CONFIRMATION OF MINUTES OF THE PREVIOUS MEETING

The minutes of the meeting held on 18 January 2023 were confirmed as a true and accurate record of proceedings.
Moved: Cr. Bell; Seconded: Cr. Okafor.
Carried.

2. BUSINESS ARISING FROM THE PREVIOUS MINUTES

2.1 Action Item 2023-01-04: Mr Foster to provide a copy of the NSW Fair Trading risk assessment for the recalled Sunbeam Appliances kettle model. Completed. The document was circulated to committee members under cover of email dated 3 February 2023.

2.2 Action Item 2023-01-09: Sergeant Nguyen to liaise with the local fire brigade regarding the preliminary report into the incident at a residence in Lismore. Sergeant Nguyen advised that the report had been received and that the cause of the fire had been consistent with an electrical fault originating in the appliance. The report had been forwarded to NSW Fair Trading for inclusion in the national incident database.

2.3 Action Item 2023-01-12: Ms Delaney to prepare a draft community awareness plan for the recall. Ms Delaney tabled a draft plan, which was considered under Item 5 of this agenda.

3. DECLARATIONS OF INTEREST

Cr. Whitfield declared a non-pecuniary interest in Item 5 (Community Awareness Program) on the grounds that her spouse was employed by a local community radio station that might be engaged to broadcast public announcements. Cr. Whitfield remained in the meeting but took no part in the decision on the selection of media partners.

No other declarations were made.

4. COMPLIANCE AUDIT OF SUNBEAM APPLIANCES – REVIEW OF FINDINGS AND CORRECTIVE ACTIONS

Mr Foster presented the final report of the compliance audit conducted by NSW Fair Trading in January 2023. The audit had been commissioned following the recall of the Sunbeam Appliances electric kettle (model SK-2100) announced on 12 January 2023.

Mr Foster summarised the audit findings as follows:

(a) The manufacturer’s traceability records for the affected production batch (August to November 2022) were incomplete. Of the 4,200 units recorded as shipped to Australian retailers, the manufacturer could account for 3,950 units. The remaining 250 units could not be traced to a specific retail outlet or consumer.

(b) The manufacturer’s consumer notification process had been found to be deficient. The initial public announcement had been made through the manufacturer’s website only, and no direct contact had been made with consumers who had registered their warranty cards. The audit recommended that the manufacturer contact all registered owners by email or letter within 14 days.

(c) The manufacturer had not provided point-of-sale notices to retailers within the required timeframe. Only 62% of known retail outlets had received the recall notice within the first week of the recall.

(d) The manufacturer’s call centre had been unable to handle the volume of enquiries in the first two weeks of the recall. The average wait time had exceeded 20 minutes, and the audit recorded 14 dropped calls per day.

Council Chambers, Level 2, 44 Harbour Street, Newcastle NSW

Ms K. Ibrahim (Acting Manager, Brisbane Testing Laboratory), Mr D. Fielding (Laboratory Quality Officer)

**5. COMMUNITY AWARENESS PROGRAM – SELECTION OF MEDIA PARTNERS**

The Committee considered the draft plan tabled by Ms Delaney at the previous meeting. Following discussion, Cr. Okafor moved that the draft plan be adopted with the amendment that the selection of media partners be deferred until the next meeting to allow for a review of the proposed engagement terms. The motion was seconded by Cr. Nguyen.

**Motion carried.**

It was resolved that the draft plan be adopted, with the selection of media partners to be considered at the next meeting. Cr. Whitfield took no part in the decision.

---

**6. ACCREDITATION EXPIRY OF BRISBANE TESTING LABORATORY – RENEWAL OPTIONS AND SERVICE CONTINUITY**

Ms Ibrahim and Mr Fielding attended the meeting for this item.

Ms Ibrahim advised the Committee that the National Association of Testing Authorities (NATA) accreditation for Brisbane Testing Laboratory (BTL) is due to expire on 31 August 2023. The laboratory currently holds accreditation for the following scopes:

- AS/NZS 60335.1 electrical appliance safety testing
- AS/NZS 60335.2.15 heating appliances
- AS/NZS 62368.1 audio/video and ICT equipment

Ms Ibrahim stated that the laboratory had submitted its application for renewal to NATA on 2 May 2023. The application was acknowledged as complete on 19 May 2023. A technical assessment is scheduled for 24 to 26 July 2023.

Mr Foster asked whether the renewal application included any changes to the scope of accreditation. Ms Ibrahim confirmed that the laboratory had applied to add a new scope for cordless appliance battery testing (AS/NZS 62133). This was a direct response to the increased volume of cordless kitchen appliances entering the market.

Cr. Nguyen asked whether the laboratory had any findings from its most recent internal audit that might affect the NATA assessment. Mr Fielding reported that the laboratory had completed an internal audit on 9 June 2023. Three minor non-conformities were identified, all relating to record keeping in the sample receiving area. Corrective actions have been implemented, and the laboratory is confident that these will be resolved before the NATA assessment.

The Committee discussed the implications for the Council’s testing program if the accreditation lapsed. Mr Foster advised that the Council relies on BTL for approximately 40% of its annual product safety testing, particularly for electrical appliances. In the event of a lapse, the Council would need to redirect testing to alternative laboratories, which would incur additional costs and likely cause delays of up to eight weeks for routine testing.

Ms Ibrahim assured the Committee that the laboratory was taking all necessary steps to ensure a successful renewal. She noted that the laboratory had not had any significant findings in its previous two NATA assessments.

Cr. Okafor asked whether the laboratory had a contingency plan in the event of a delay in the NATA assessment. Ms Ibrahim confirmed that the laboratory had approached two alternative NATA-accredited laboratories in Queensland to act as overflow providers. A memorandum of understanding had been drafted with one of these laboratories.

**MINUTES OF THE CONSUMER PRODUCT SAFETY COMMITTEE**

**Meeting No. 2020-11-30**

**Held via videoconference, 30 November 2020, 9:30 am**

**1. Attendance**

Present: Cr. A. Nguyen (Chair), Cr. P. Okafor, Cr. L. Tran, Ms. R. Ibrahim (Manager, Laboratory Services), Mr. J. Fielding (Senior Compliance Officer), Ms. S. Patel (Consumer Liaison Officer), Mr. D. Foster (Technical Officer), Mr. T. Whitlam (Secretariat).

Apologies: Cr. M. Delgado, Cr. S. Romano.

The Chair declared a quorum.

**2. Confirmation of Previous Minutes**

The minutes of the meeting held on 26 October 2020 were confirmed as a true and accurate record. Moved: Cr. Okafor. Seconded: Cr. Tran. Motion carried.

**3. Business Arising from Previous Minutes**

3.1 Item 5.2 (Recall of cordless kettles, recall no. 2020-10-14): Mr. Fielding reported that the supplier had submitted its corrective action report on 13 November 2020. The report has been forwarded to the Office of Fair Trading for review. The Committee noted the update.

3.2 Item 6.1 (Annual testing schedule): Ms. Ibrahim confirmed that the revised schedule for 2021 has been circulated. The schedule incorporates the additional testing requirements arising from the new mandatory standard for toasters. Noted.

**4. Complaint Handling Protocol – Proposed Revision**

4.1 The Chair invited Mr. Fielding to present the proposed revision of the Complaint Handling Protocol (document ref. CHP-2019/02). Mr. Fielding noted that the current protocol had been in operation since February 2019 and that a review was due.

4.2 Mr. Fielding summarised the key changes:

- The definition of a "serious complaint" has been expanded to include any incident involving a suspected fire, electric shock, or injury requiring medical attention. The previous definition only covered incidents involving fire or electric shock.
- The response time for acknowledging a serious complaint has been reduced from five business days to three business days.
- A new requirement has been added for the Consumer Liaison Officer to conduct a follow-up interview with the complainant within ten business days of the initial report, where the complainant consents.
- The protocol now includes a clear escalation pathway to the Office of Fair Trading for complaints that indicate an imminent safety risk.
- A new appendix has been added with a standardised complaint form, which will replace the various informal methods currently used to receive complaints.

4.3 Ms. Patel queried the resource implications of the reduced acknowledgement time. Mr. Fielding advised that the Complaints Register is currently managed by two officers who spend approximately 0.2 FTE each on complaint handling. The reduced response time is expected to increase the workload by no more than 0.05 FTE, which can be absorbed within existing staffing. The follow-up interview requirement is expected to add a further 0.1 FTE to Ms. Patel's duties.

4.4 Cr. Tran asked whether the revised protocol would affect the Council's reporting obligations to the Australian Competition and Consumer Commission (ACCC) under the Consumer Goods (Product Safety) standards. Mr. Fielding confirmed that the protocol does not change the statutory reporting thresholds; it only strengthens the internal handling of complaints that meet those thresholds.

4.5 Cr. Okafor asked how the revised protocol would be communicated to the public. Ms. Patel advised that the updated protocol would be published on the Council's website, and that a notice would be included with the next quarterly consumer newsletter. She also proposed that a short information sheet be prepared for distribution at the Council's community engagement events.

Moved: Cr. Okafor; Seconded: Cr. Whitfield. **Motion carried.**

2.1 Action item CLO-2023-014 (Consumer Liaison Officer to draft information sheet on the revised Complaints Handling Protocol). Ms. Patel advised the draft is complete and has been forwarded to the Communications Team for design. Expected publication date is late January 2024. **Action closed.**

2.2 Action item CM-2023-022 (Compliance Manager to provide a summary of product recall notifications received in November). Mr. Fielding tabled the summary. Four notifications were received from the ACCC during November, covering the following product categories: one children's toy, one electrical appliance, one cosmetic, and one bicycle accessory. No notifications were received for products supplied by local retailers. **Noted.**

**3. Correspondence**
A letter was received from a local consumer advocacy group regarding the clarity of safety information on children's nightwear. The group requested that the Committee consider a public awareness campaign. Mr. Fielding noted that the ACCC has published guidance on this matter and that the Council could link to this resource on its website. The Committee agreed to add this item to the agenda for the February 2024 meeting. **Noted.**

**4. Reports**

4.1 **Complaints Handling Protocol – Implementation Update (Ms. Patel)**
Ms. Patel reported that the revised Complaints Handling Protocol, adopted at the November meeting, has been in operation for four weeks. The updated definition of a serious complaint now covers any incident involving fire, electric shock, or injury requiring medical attention, aligning with the broader scope agreed at the previous meeting.

A total of 31 complaints were received during November. Of these, two were classified as serious under the revised definition. Both were acknowledged within the new three-business-day timeframe. One complainant consented to a follow-up interview, which was conducted on 8 December. The other complainant declined.

Ms. Patel noted that the new requirement for a follow-up interview within ten business days has added an estimated 0.1 FTE to her workload, as anticipated. The overall workload increase from the reduced acknowledgement time remains within the 0.05 FTE estimate provided by Mr. Fielding. No additional staffing has been required.

The standardised complaint form has been well received by both staff and complainants. The form is now available on the Council website, and a notice has been included in the December edition of the quarterly consumer newsletter. A small number of printed copies have been distributed at recent community engagement events.

Cr. Tran thanked Ms. Patel for the update and asked whether any complaints had been escalated to the Office of Fair Trading under the new pathway. Ms. Patel advised that no escalations had been required during the reporting period, as neither serious complaint indicated an imminent safety risk. **Noted.**
